c1-gen-0062: After these things, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision. Let's read Genesis 15:1.
c2-gen-0021: God gave food to the man and woman, and to every beast, bird, and creeping thing too. Let's look at Genesis 1:29 and 30 together.
c2-gen-0022: On the way up the mountain, Isaac asked his father where the lamb was. Let's read Genesis 22:8 and 14.
c2-gen-0023: God set His rainbow in the cloud. Let's hear what He says about it in Genesis 9:15 and 16.
c3-gen-0003: Jacob said Judah's brothers would praise him and bow before him, and yes, this lion is listening closely. Let's open Genesis 49:8 and 10.
c3-gen-0004: God told Abram to count the stars, if he could. Let's read Genesis 15:5 and 22:17.
c3-gen-0005: God promised that in Abram all the families of the earth would be blessed. Let's turn to Genesis 12:3 and 22:18.
c3-gen-0006: Way back in the garden, God put enmity between the serpent and the woman. Let's read Genesis 3:15 and 22:17.
c1-gen-0063: The herdsmen of Abram and Lot were quarreling. Let's hear Abram in Genesis 13:8.
c2-gen-0024: Abram would not take even a thread or a sandal strap from the king of Sodom. Let's check Genesis 14:22 and 23.
c2-gen-0025: Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram. Let's read Genesis 14:18 and 20.
c2-gen-0026: Jacob asked Laban, "Why then have you deceived me?" Let's dig into Genesis 29:25 and 26.
c3-gen-0007: Jacob's household put away their foreign gods before heading to Bethel. Let's read Genesis 35:2, 4, and 5.
c3-gen-0008: God spoke a big promise over Jacob, and long before that, a promise about Sarah. Read Genesis 17:16 and 35:11 with me.
c3-gen-0009: Sarai, Rebekah, and Rachel all knew the ache of waiting for a child. Let's read Genesis 11:30, 25:21, and 30:22.
c3-gen-0010: Jacob once took Esau's birthright for bread and stew. Let's see how their story turned, in Genesis 25:33, 25:34, and 35:29.
c1-exo-0022: At Sinai, God reminded Israel what He had done to the Egyptians. Let's go to Exodus 19:4.
c2-exo-0019: The people trembled at the thunder and the trumpet, and Moses told them not to fear. Let's read Exodus 20:20.
c2-exo-0020: The people begged Moses to speak to them instead of God, and they stood afar off. Let's look closely at Exodus 20:19 and 21.
c2-exo-0021: Picture your enemy's ox or donkey wandering off down the road. Let's read Exodus 23:4 and 5.
c3-exo-0003: God said He would not drive out the land's peoples in one year. Let's look at Exodus 23:29 and 30 together.
c3-exo-0004: God told Israel twice not to oppress a stranger, because of their own past in Egypt. Let's read Exodus 22:21 and 23:9.
c3-exo-0005: At Sinai the people made a promise, and they made it again when the covenant was sealed. Let's open Exodus 19:8 and 24:7.
c3-exo-0006: God made promises to those who obey His voice and keep His covenant. Let's read Exodus 19:5 and 23:22.
c1-lev-0003: In the fiftieth year, Israel had something to announce throughout the land. Let's turn to Leviticus 25:10.
c2-lev-0007: God knew the people would ask, "What shall we eat in the seventh year?" Let's read Leviticus 25:20 and 21.
c2-lev-0008: God said the land must not be sold permanently. Let's hear why in Leviticus 25:23 and 24.
c2-lev-0009: God commanded honest scales and honest weights. Let's check Leviticus 19:35 and 36.
c3-lev-0001: Every Sabbath, the bread was set in order before the LORD. Let's read Leviticus 24:8 and 9.
c3-lev-0002: Twice, Leviticus tells Israel to fear their God. Let's dig into Leviticus 19:32 and 25:36.
c3-lev-0003: Every seventh year, the land was to have a sabbath of solemn rest. Let's read Leviticus 25:4, 26:34, and 26:35.
c3-lev-0004: God told Israel how to treat those who dwell among them, and a brother who falls on hard times. Read Leviticus 19:34 and 25:35 with me.
c1-num-0003: On Mount Hor, Moses removed Aaron's priestly garments. Let's read Numbers 20:26 and 28.
c2-num-0008: Joshua said, "Moses my lord, forbid them!" Let's hear Moses answer in Numbers 11:28 and 29.
c2-num-0009: Miriam and Aaron questioned whether the LORD spoke only through Moses. Let's go to Numbers 12:2 and 3.
c2-num-0010: When the plague began, Aaron ran into the assembly with incense. Let's read Numbers 16:47 and 48.
c3-num-0001: Korah's company told Moses and Aaron, "You take too much upon yourselves." Let's look closely at Numbers 16:3 and 7.
c3-num-0002: Moses told Korah the LORD would show whom He chooses. Let's read Numbers 16:5, 17:5, and 17:8.
c3-num-0003: God took of the Spirit on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. Let's look at Numbers 11:17 and 27:20 together.
c3-num-0004: Moses called on God by a special title after Korah's rebellion, and again when he asked for a leader. Let's read Numbers 16:22 and 27:16.
c1-deu-0005: Moses died in the land of Moab. Let's open Deuteronomy 34:6.
c2-deu-0013: Moses told Israel's judges not to show partiality or be afraid of any man. Let's read Deuteronomy 1:17.
c2-deu-0014: Moses pleaded to cross over and see the good land. Let's turn to Deuteronomy 3:25 and 26.
c2-deu-0015: Israel was the least of all peoples, yet the LORD chose them. Let's read Deuteronomy 7:7 and 8.
c3-deu-0001: Back in Egypt, crops were watered by foot. Let's check Deuteronomy 11:10 and 11.
c3-deu-0002: Moses wrote down the law and handed it to the priests, and a future king was to copy it out. Let's read Deuteronomy 17:18, 17:20, and 31:9.
c3-deu-0003: God told Moses to go up Pisgah, but not to cross the Jordan. Let's dig into Deuteronomy 3:27 and 34:4.
c3-deu-0004: Moses told Israel to teach God's words to their children. Let's read Deuteronomy 11:19 and 31:13.
c1-1ch-0001: Saul did not keep the word of the LORD, and he consulted a medium. Read First Chronicles 10:13 and 14 with me.
c2-1ch-0001: David lived in a house of cedar while the ark sat under tent curtains. Let's read First Chronicles 17:1 and 2.
c2-1ch-0002: David was told he would not build a house for God's name. Let's go to First Chronicles 22:8 and 9.
c2-1ch-0003: Gad brought David three choices of judgment. Let's read First Chronicles 21:12 and 13.
c3-1ch-0001: David built an altar, called on the LORD, and was answered from heaven. Let's look closely at First Chronicles 21:26 and 27.
c3-1ch-0002: David took much trouble to prepare gold, silver, bronze, and iron for the house. Let's read First Chronicles 22:14 and 29:14.
c3-1ch-0003: God told David, "You shall not build Me a house to dwell in." Let's look at First Chronicles 17:4 and 28:3 together.
c3-1ch-0004: David told Solomon that the LORD searches all hearts. Let's read First Chronicles 28:9 and 29:17.
c1-1ch-0002: David promised that whoever attacked the Jebusites first would be chief and captain. Let's open First Chronicles 11:6.
c2-1ch-0004: Three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp for water from the well of Bethlehem. Let's read First Chronicles 11:18 and 19.
c2-1ch-0005: Day by day, men came to David until it was a great army. Let's turn to First Chronicles 12:22 and 32.
c2-1ch-0006: David was afraid to bring the ark into the City of David. Let's read First Chronicles 13:13 and 14.
c3-1ch-0005: Facing the Syrians and the people of Ammon, two brothers agreed to help each other. Let's check First Chronicles 19:12 and 13.
c3-1ch-0006: David proposed bringing back the ark, but the first attempt went wrong. Let's read First Chronicles 13:3 and 15:13.
c3-1ch-0007: The first time, the ark rode on a new cart from the house of Abinadab. Let's dig into First Chronicles 13:7 and 15:15.
c3-1ch-0008: David became great because the LORD was with him. Let's read First Chronicles 11:9 and 18:6.
c1-2ch-0001: A great multitude came against Judah, and Jahaziel the Levite stood up in the assembly. Read Second Chronicles 20:15 with me.
c2-2ch-0002: At the temple dedication, Solomon stood and then knelt where all Israel could see him. Let's read Second Chronicles 6:12 and 13.
c2-2ch-0003: Jehoshaphat admitted Judah had no power against the multitude and did not know what to do. Let's go to Second Chronicles 20:3 and 12.
c2-2ch-0004: Judah marched out into the Wilderness of Tekoa, and Jehoshaphat called them to believe in the LORD. Let's read Second Chronicles 20:20 and 21.
c3-2ch-0001: King Asa's land had no war for years, and then a huge army came against Judah. Let's look closely at Second Chronicles 14:6 and 11.
c3-2ch-0002: God warned what would happen if Israel turned to idols, and long afterward the house of God was burned. Let's read Second Chronicles 7:20 and 36:19.
c3-2ch-0003: A king in deep affliction humbled himself greatly and prayed. Let's look at Second Chronicles 7:14, 33:12, and 33:13 together.
c3-2ch-0004: Solomon asked God to hear from heaven, and generations later another king prayed for worshipers who were not cleansed. Let's read Second Chronicles 6:21 and 30:20.
c1-2ch-0002: In the eighth year of his reign, King Josiah was still young. Let's open Second Chronicles 34:3.
c2-2ki-0016: Josiah had the temple money handed straight to the workmen repairing it. Let's read Second Kings 22:7.
c2-2ch-0005: Josiah sent Hilkiah and others to ask the LORD about the words of the book that was found. Let's turn to Second Chronicles 34:21 and 22.
c2-2ki-0017: Josiah read all the words of the Book of the Covenant to the people at the temple. Let's read Second Kings 23:2 and 3.
c3-2ch-0005: Getting ready for the Passover, Josiah spoke to the Levites who taught all Israel. Let's check Second Chronicles 35:2 and 3.
c3-2ki-0001: Josiah did not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. Let's read Second Kings 22:2 and 23:25.
c3-2ki-0002: Josiah feared that the LORD's wrath was great against Judah. Let's dig into Second Kings 22:13 and 23:26.
c3-2ch-0006: Josiah made a covenant before the LORD and then kept a Passover. Let's read Second Chronicles 34:31 and 35:18.
c1-ecc-0001: The Preacher says two are better than one. Read Ecclesiastes 4:12 with me.
c2-ecc-0001: All the rivers run into the sea, the Preacher notices. Let's read Ecclesiastes 1:7.
c2-ecc-0002: There is a season for everything and a time for every purpose under heaven. Let's go to Ecclesiastes 3:1 and 11.
c2-ecc-0003: "Do not be rash with your mouth," the Preacher warns, for God is in heaven. Let's read Ecclesiastes 5:2 and 3.
c3-ecc-0001: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong. Let's look closely at Ecclesiastes 9:11 and 12.
c3-ecc-0002: The Preacher says enjoying good in one's labor comes from the hand of God. Let's read Ecclesiastes 2:24 and 3:13.
c3-ecc-0003: The Preacher tells the young man to rejoice in his youth, and to know that judgment is coming. Let's look at Ecclesiastes 11:9 and 12:1 together.
c3-ecc-0004: Ecclesiastes opens with "Vanity of vanities, all is vanity." Let's read Ecclesiastes 1:2 and 12:13.
c1-sng-0001: In the Song, the speaker describes herself with two flowers. Let's open Song of Solomon 2:1.
c2-sng-0001: Something was spoiling the vines while they had tender grapes. Let's read Song of Solomon 2:15.
c2-sng-0002: Her beloved says, "Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away." Let's turn to Song of Solomon 2:10 and 11.
c2-sng-0003: The bride says, "My beloved is mine, and I am his." Let's read Song of Solomon 2:16 and 17.
c3-sng-0001: The bride charges the daughters of Jerusalem not to stir up or awaken love. Let's check Song of Solomon 2:7 and 5:8.
c3-sng-0002: Solomon's vineyard at Baal Hamon brought in a thousand silver coins from each keeper. Let's read Song of Solomon 8:7 and 8:11.
c3-sng-0003: "How much better than wine is your love," the beloved says. Let's dig into Song of Solomon 4:10 and 8:6.
c3-sng-0004: The bride says her beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Let's read Song of Solomon 2:9 and 8:14.
c1-lam-0001: Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. Read Lamentations 3:22 and 23 with me.
c2-lam-0001: Lamentations opens by mourning a city that was once full of people. Let's read Lamentations 1:1.
c2-lam-0002: The writer says, "Therefore I hope in Him!" Let's go to Lamentations 3:24 and 25.
c2-lam-0003: The writer calls, "Let us lift our hearts and hands to God in heaven." Let's read Lamentations 3:40 and 41.
c3-lam-0001: The Lord will not cast off forever, and though He causes grief, He will show compassion. Let's look closely at Lamentations 3:31, 32, and 33.
c3-lam-0002: Jerusalem wept because her comforter was far away. Let's read Lamentations 1:16 and 3:57.
c3-lam-0003: Mount Zion lay desolate, yet the writer still lifted his eyes to the LORD. Let's look at Lamentations 3:22 and 5:19 together.
c3-lam-0004: Mockers once asked if Jerusalem was the city called "The perfection of beauty." Let's read Lamentations 2:15 and 4:2.
c1-hos-0001: When the LORD began to speak by Hosea, He told him to take a wife. Let's open Hosea 1:3.
c2-hos-0001: The LORD remembered loving Israel when Israel was a child. Let's read Hosea 11:1.
c2-hos-0002: The LORD says He will lead her into the wilderness, speak comfort to her, and give her vineyards. Let's turn to Hosea 2:14 and 15.
c2-hos-0003: "In that day," says the LORD, she will call Him "My Husband." Let's read Hosea 2:16 and 17.
c3-hos-0001: God says He taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by their arms. Let's check Hosea 11:3 and 4.
c3-hos-0002: Hosea's son was named Lo-Ammi, "For you are not My people." Let's read Hosea 1:9 and 2:23.
c3-hos-0003: God cries out, "How can I give you up, Ephraim?" Let's dig into Hosea 11:8 and 14:8.
c3-hos-0004: Hosea calls, "O Israel, return to the LORD your God." Let's read Hosea 3:5 and 14:1.
c1-hos-0002: Hosea says Ephraim has mixed himself among the peoples. Read Hosea 7:8 with me.
c2-hos-0004: The LORD asks, "O Ephraim, what shall I do to you?" Let's read Hosea 6:4.
c2-hos-0005: "They sow the wind," Hosea says about Israel's folly. Let's go to Hosea 8:7 and 10:13.
c2-hos-0006: Israel would not return to the LORD or seek Him, and ran to foreign powers instead. Let's read Hosea 7:10 and 11.
c3-hos-0005: Hosea urges, "Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy." Let's look closely at Hosea 10:12 and 12:6.
c3-hos-0006: The people say, "Come, and let us return to the LORD; for He has torn, but He will heal us." Let's read Hosea 5:15 and 6:1.
c3-hos-0007: The LORD says He desires mercy and not sacrifice. Let's look at Hosea 6:6 and 13:4 together.
c3-hos-0008: God says He found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. Let's read Hosea 9:10 and 13:5.
c1-jol-0001: After locusts ruined the land, Joel called the people to return to the LORD. Let's open Joel 2:13.
c2-jol-0001: A nation laid waste the LORD's vine and stripped His fig tree bare. Let's read Joel 1:7.
c2-jol-0002: The LORD says, "I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh." Let's turn to Joel 2:28 and 29.
c2-jol-0003: With the locusts and the day of the LORD at hand, Joel told the priests, "Consecrate a fast." Let's read Joel 1:14 and 15.
c3-jol-0001: The LORD will roar from Zion, and the heavens and earth will shake; now that is a roar. Let's check Joel 3:16 and 17.
c3-jol-0002: "Blow the trumpet in Zion," Joel calls, for the day of the LORD is coming. Let's read Joel 2:1 and 3:14.
c3-jol-0003: Four kinds of locusts each ate what the one before had left. Let's dig into Joel 1:4 and 2:25.
c3-jol-0004: The sun and moon will be darkened before the day of the LORD. Let's read Joel 2:31 and 3:15.
c1-amo-0001: The book of Amos opens by telling us who Amos was before he spoke for the LORD. Read Amos 1:1 with me.
c2-amo-0001: The LORD says Israel sold the righteous for silver. Let's read Amos 2:6.
c2-amo-0002: Amos asks a chain of questions, starting with "Can two walk together." Let's go to Amos 3:3 and 4.
c2-amo-0003: The LORD says He will destroy the winter house along with the summer house. Let's read Amos 3:14 and 15.
c3-amo-0001: The LORD lists the hardships He sent, like lack of bread and withheld rain. Let's look closely at Amos 4:6 and 8.
c3-amo-0002: The LORD says, "You only have I known of all the families of the earth." Let's read Amos 3:2 and 4:12.
c3-amo-0003: "The LORD roars from Zion," Amos begins, and you know I love a good roar. Let's look at Amos 1:2 and 3:8 together.
c3-amo-0004: The nations were called to the mountains of Samaria to see the oppressed within her. Let's read Amos 3:9 and 4:1.
c1-amo-0002: In a vision, the Lord stood with something in His hand and asked, "Amos, what do you see?" Let's open Amos 7:7 and 8.
c2-amo-0004: "Take away from Me the noise of your songs," the LORD says. Let's read Amos 5:23 and 24.
c2-amo-0005: The LORD told Israel to stay away from Bethel, Gilgal, and Beersheba. Let's turn to Amos 5:4 and 5.
c2-amo-0006: Amaziah the priest told Amos, "Go, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah." Let's read Amos 7:12 and 13.
c3-amo-0005: Some lay on beds of ivory, drank wine from bowls, and anointed themselves with the best ointments. Let's check Amos 6:4 and 6.
c3-amo-0006: In a vision of locusts, Amos pleaded, "O Lord GOD, forgive, I pray!" Let's read Amos 7:2 and 9:8.
c3-amo-0007: Amos warned that the day of the LORD would be darkness, and not light. Let's dig into Amos 5:18 and 8:9.
c3-amo-0008: Amos lamented that the virgin of Israel had fallen, with no one to raise her up. Let's read Amos 5:2 and 9:11.
c1-mic-0001: The word of the LORD came to Micah in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. Read Micah 1:1 with me.
c2-mic-0002: In the latter days, nations shall beat their swords into plowshares. Let's read Micah 4:3.
c2-mic-0003: Micah says everyone shall sit under his vine and under his fig tree. Let's go to Micah 4:4 and 5.
c2-mic-0004: Jerusalem's heads judged for a bribe, and her priests taught for pay. Let's read Micah 3:11 and 12.
c3-mic-0001: Micah speaks of the One who will be Ruler in Israel. Let's look closely at Micah 5:2 and 3.
c3-mic-0002: Micah condemned those who plotted evil on their beds, and he mourned that the faithful man had perished. Let's read Micah 2:1 and 7:2.
c3-mic-0003: Zion was plowed like a field, yet many nations would say, "He will teach us His ways." Let's look at Micah 3:12 and 4:2 together.
c3-mic-0004: The prince asked for gifts and the judge sought a bribe, but the coming One would feed His flock. Let's read Micah 5:4 and 7:3.
c1-mic-0002: "He has shown you, O man, what is good." Let's open Micah 6:8.
c2-mic-0005: Micah says the LORD will again have compassion on us and subdue our iniquities. Let's read Micah 7:19.
c2-mic-0006: "Who is a God like You, pardoning iniquity?" Micah asks. Let's turn to Micah 7:17 and 18.
c2-mic-0007: "O My people, what have I done to you?" the LORD asks. Let's read Micah 6:3 and 4.
c3-mic-0005: "Do not rejoice over me, my enemy," Micah says. Let's check Micah 7:7 and 8.
c3-mic-0006: The LORD promised to redeem the daughter of Zion from the hand of her enemies. Let's read Micah 4:10 and 7:15.
c3-mic-0007: The LORD had a complaint against His people, yet Micah closes with what God swore to the fathers. Let's dig into Micah 6:2 and 7:20.
c3-mic-0008: The remnant of Jacob will be like dew from the LORD among many peoples. Let's read Micah 4:7 and 5:7.
c1-hab-0001: Habakkuk opens by complaining that the LORD does not seem to hear or save. Read Habakkuk 1:1 and 2 with me.
c2-hab-0001: Habakkuk waited on the rampart, and the LORD told him, "Write the vision." Let's read Habakkuk 2:2.
c2-hab-0002: "Behold the proud, his soul is not upright in him." Let's go to Habakkuk 2:3 and 4.
c2-hab-0003: Habakkuk says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD. Let's read Habakkuk 2:13 and 14.
c3-hab-0001: Habakkuk mocks idols with no breath at all, then says, "But the LORD is in His holy temple." Let's look closely at Habakkuk 2:19 and 20.
c3-hab-0002: Habakkuk called God "O Rock," and later prayed for Him to revive His work. Let's read Habakkuk 1:12 and 3:2.
c3-hab-0003: Habakkuk began by asking, "Why do You show me iniquity?" Let's look at Habakkuk 1:3, 3:17, and 3:18 together.
c3-hab-0004: Habakkuk stood his watch on the rampart, and at the end he says, "The LORD God is my strength." Let's read Habakkuk 2:1 and 3:19.
c1-hag-0001: The LORD of hosts told the people, "Go up to the mountains." Let's open Haggai 1:8.
c2-hag-0001: The people said the time had not yet come to build the LORD's house. Let's read Haggai 1:4.
c2-hag-0002: "Consider your ways!" They had sown much and brought in little. Let's turn to Haggai 1:5 and 6.
c2-hag-0003: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant obeyed and feared the presence of the LORD. Let's read Haggai 1:12 and 13.
c3-hag-0001: The LORD asked, "Is this not in your eyes as nothing?" Let's check Haggai 2:3 and 9.
c3-hag-0002: The people had said, "The time has not come," but then the temple work started again. Let's read Haggai 1:2 and 2:19.
c3-hag-0003: The LORD called for a drought on the land. Let's dig into Haggai 1:11 and 2:17.
c3-hag-0004: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, governor of Judah. Let's read Haggai 1:14 and 2:23.
c1-zec-0001: Zechariah's first message: "Return to Me," says the LORD of hosts. Read Zechariah 1:2 and 3 with me.
c2-zec-0001: In Zechariah's first night vision, a man rode a red horse. Let's read Zechariah 1:8.
c2-zec-0002: "Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon." Let's go to Zechariah 2:7 and 8.
c2-zec-0003: Joshua the high priest stood before the Angel in filthy garments. Let's read Zechariah 3:3 and 4.
c3-zec-0001: The angel gave Zerubbabel the word of the LORD: "Not by might nor by power." Let's look closely at Zechariah 4:6 and 7.
c3-zec-0002: The people were told, "Let your hands be strong," as the temple was built. Let's read Zechariah 4:10 and 8:9.
c3-zec-0003: The LORD says, "I am zealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great zeal." Let's look at Zechariah 1:14 and 8:3 together.
c3-zec-0004: Many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day. Let's read Zechariah 2:11 and 8:23.
c1-zec-0002: Zechariah calls, "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion!" and announces her coming King. Let's open Zechariah 9:9.
c2-zec-0004: The LORD promised to free His people from the waterless pit. Let's read Zechariah 9:11 and 12.
c2-zec-0005: Zechariah fed the flock for slaughter and took two staffs, and one he called Beauty. Let's turn to Zechariah 11:7 and 10.
c2-zec-0006: Jerusalem would be like a cup of drunkenness to the peoples around her. Let's read Zechariah 12:2 and 3.
c3-zec-0005: After a great mourning in Jerusalem, the LORD provides for the house of David. Let's check Zechariah 12:11 and 13:1.
c3-zec-0006: One day the LORD shall be King over all the earth. Let's read Zechariah 13:9 and 14:9.
c3-zec-0007: The coming King shall speak peace to the nations. Let's dig into Zechariah 9:10 and 12:10.
c3-zec-0008: The LORD will cut off the names of the idols from the land. Let's read Zechariah 13:2 and 14:20.
c1-jos-0016: Before the battle with Jabin and the northern kings, the LORD gave Joshua orders about their horses. Read Joshua 11:6 with me.
c2-jos-0008: The LORD told Joshua to appoint cities of refuge for someone who killed a person by accident. Let's read Joshua 20:2 and 3.
c2-jos-0009: At Gilgal, Caleb reminded Joshua of the day Moses sent him from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land. Let's go to Joshua 14:6 and 7.
c2-jos-0010: Phinehas and the rulers were satisfied, and Reuben and Gad named the great altar at the border. Let's read Joshua 22:33 and 34.
c3-jos-0003: Joshua sent the eastern tribes home with a charge to love the LORD and walk in all His ways. Let's look closely at Joshua 22:4 and 5.
c3-jos-0004: The LORD gave Israel what He had sworn to their fathers. Let's read Joshua 13:1 and 21:43.
c3-jos-0005: Caleb asked for the mountain where the Anakim lived. Let's look at Joshua 11:22 and 14:12 together.
c3-jos-0006: Phinehas and the rulers heard the words of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, and it pleased them. Let's read Joshua 20:4 and 22:30.
c1-2sa-0015: Absalom rose early and stood beside the way, meeting everyone who came to the king with a lawsuit. Let's open Second Samuel 15:2 and 4.
c2-2sa-0003: Someone told David that Ahithophel had joined Absalom's conspiracy. Let's read Second Samuel 15:31.
c2-2sa-0004: David told Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner, to go back. Let's turn to Second Samuel 15:19 and 21.
c2-2sa-0005: Shimei cursed David, and Abishai wanted to stop him. Let's read Second Samuel 16:10 and 11.
c3-2sa-0001: Hushai argued against chasing David right away. Let's check Second Samuel 17:7 and 8.
c3-2sa-0002: David and his servants fled Jerusalem in a hurry, and friends at Mahanaim brought honey, curds, sheep, and cheese. Let's read Second Samuel 15:14 and 17:29.
c3-2sa-0003: Hushai passed along what had been advised in Absalom's council. Let's dig into Second Samuel 15:32 and 17:15.
c3-2sa-0004: David hoped the LORD would look on his affliction. Let's read Second Samuel 16:12 and 18:27.
c1-2sa-0016: A man of great stature, born to the giant, showed up for battle. Read Second Samuel 21:20 with me.

c3-heb-0002: Christ says, "To do Your will, O God." Let's read Hebrews 5:7 and 10:7.
c3-heb-0003: His offering was once for all. Let's dig into Hebrews 7:27 and 9:12.
c3-heb-0004: Our High Priest is seated beside the throne of the Majesty. Let's read Hebrews 8:1 and 10:14.
c1-heb-0004: Hebrews says we must give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard. Read Hebrews 2:1 with me.
c2-heb-0010: The writer asks a chain of questions about the people who left Egypt with Moses. Let's read Hebrews 3:16 and 18.
c2-heb-0011: God's word is sharper than any two-edged sword. Let's go to Hebrews 4:12 and 13.
c2-heb-0012: Hebrews says not to forget to entertain strangers. Let's read Hebrews 13:2 and 3.
c3-heb-0005: Our human fathers corrected us, and so does the Father of spirits. Let's look closely at Hebrews 12:9 and 10.
c3-heb-0006: Hebrews urges believers to exhort one another. Let's read Hebrews 3:13, 10:24, and 10:25.
c3-heb-0007: We have need of endurance after doing the will of God. Let's look at Hebrews 6:12 and 10:36 together.
c3-heb-0008: Hebrews says not to cast away your confidence, which has great reward. Let's read Hebrews 3:14 and 10:35.
c1-rev-0007: When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, John saw the souls of those slain for the word of God. Let's open Revelation 6:9.
c2-rev-0020: John took the little book from the angel's hand and ate it. Let's read Revelation 10:9 and 10.
c2-rev-0021: The souls cried out, asking how long until God would avenge their blood. Let's turn to Revelation 6:10 and 11.
c2-rev-0022: The angel standing on the sea and on the land raised his hand to heaven. Let's read Revelation 10:5 and 6.
c3-rev-0002: Kings, great men, slaves, and free men all fled to the caves of the mountains. Let's check Revelation 6:15 and 16.
c3-rev-0003: When the seventh angel sounded, loud voices rang out in heaven. Let's read Revelation 6:15 and 11:15.
c3-rev-0004: One of the living creatures spoke with a voice like thunder. Let's dig into Revelation 6:1 and 10:4.
c3-rev-0005: People on the earth cried that the great day of His wrath had come. Let's read Revelation 6:17, 11:16, and 11:17.
c1-col-0001: The Colossians first learned the good news from a dear fellow servant. Read Colossians 1:7 with me.
c2-col-0001: Paul sends greetings from Luke and Demas. Let's read Colossians 4:14.
c2-col-0002: They will receive the reward of the inheritance from the Lord. Let's go to Colossians 3:23 and 24.
c2-col-0003: "Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle." Let's read Colossians 2:21 and 22.
c3-col-0001: Paul says to set your mind on things above, not on things on the earth. Let's look closely at Colossians 3:2 and 3.
c3-col-0002: Principalities and powers were created through Him and for Him. Let's read Colossians 1:16 and 2:15.
c3-col-0003: In Him everything holds together. Let's look at Colossians 1:17 and 3:11 together.
c3-col-0004: Paul urges the Colossians to continue in the faith, steady and unmoved. Let's read Colossians 1:23 and 2:5.
c1-1th-0001: Others told how the Thessalonians turned to God to serve the living and true God. Let's open First Thessalonians 1:9.
c2-1th-0001: Paul says they were gentle among the Thessalonians. Let's read First Thessalonians 2:7.
c2-1th-0002: Paul longed with great desire to see the Thessalonians face to face. Let's turn to First Thessalonians 2:17 and 18.
c2-1th-0003: Paul could hardly find thanks enough to give God for all his joy over them. Let's read First Thessalonians 3:9 and 10.
c3-1th-0001: God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus. Let's check First Thessalonians 4:13 and 14.
c3-1th-0002: Paul prays that the Lord would make them abound in love to one another. Let's read First Thessalonians 3:12 and 4:9.
c3-1th-0003: Jesus delivers us from the wrath to come. Let's dig into First Thessalonians 1:10 and 5:9.
c3-1th-0004: Paul urges them to walk worthy of God, who calls them into His own kingdom. Let's read First Thessalonians 2:12 and 4:12.
c1-2th-0001: Paul repeats a command he gave while he was with them: "If anyone will not work." Read Second Thessalonians 3:10 with me.
c2-2th-0001: Paul closes with a greeting written by his own hand. Let's read Second Thessalonians 3:17.
c2-2th-0002: Paul did not want them shaken in mind or troubled by spirit, word, or letter. Let's go to Second Thessalonians 2:1 and 2.
c2-2th-0003: Paul says not to keep company with anyone who does not obey the word in this letter. Let's read Second Thessalonians 3:14 and 15.
c3-2th-0001: Paul wanted to make himself an example for them to follow. Let's look closely at Second Thessalonians 3:8 and 9.
c3-2th-0002: Paul prays that the Lord of peace would give them peace always in every way. Let's read Second Thessalonians 2:16 and 3:16.
c3-2th-0003: They were suffering so that they might be counted worthy of God's kingdom. Let's look at Second Thessalonians 1:5 and 2:14 together.
c3-2th-0004: Paul says, "we also pray always for you," and then asks them to pray for him too. Let's read Second Thessalonians 1:11 and 3:1.
c1-1ti-0001: Paul gives a faithful saying, worthy of all acceptance. Let's open First Timothy 1:15.
c2-1ti-0001: Paul tells Timothy, "Let no one despise your youth." Let's read First Timothy 4:12.
c2-1ti-0002: Children should first learn to show piety at home. Let's turn to First Timothy 5:4 and 8.
c2-1ti-0003: We brought nothing into this world, and we can carry nothing out. Let's read First Timothy 6:6 and 7.
c3-1ti-0001: Paul tells Timothy to give attention to reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine. Let's check First Timothy 4:13 and 15.
c3-1ti-0002: Paul charges Timothy to fight the fight of faith. Let's read First Timothy 1:19 and 6:12.
c3-1ti-0003: We trust in the living God, the Savior of all men. Let's dig into First Timothy 3:15 and 4:10.
c3-1ti-0004: Paul recalls the prophecies made earlier concerning Timothy. Let's read First Timothy 1:18 and 4:14.
c1-tit-0001: Paul left Titus behind to set things in order and appoint elders in every city. Read Titus 1:5 with me.
c2-tit-0001: Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus. Let's read Titus 3:12.
c2-tit-0002: Paul tells Titus to show himself a pattern of good works. Let's go to Titus 2:7 and 8.
c2-tit-0003: Paul tells Titus to avoid foolish disputes, genealogies, and strivings about the law. Let's read Titus 3:9 and 10.
c3-tit-0001: He gave Himself for us to redeem us from every lawless deed. Let's look closely at Titus 2:13 and 14.
c3-tit-0002: The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all. Let's read Titus 2:11, 3:4, and 3:5.
c3-tit-0003: Paul speaks of becoming heirs, justified by His grace. Let's look at Titus 1:2 and 3:7 together.
c3-tit-0004: Paul calls Titus a true son in their common faith. Let's read Titus 1:4 and 2:15.
c1-2pe-0001: Peter writes that the Lord showed him something about what lay ahead. Let's open Second Peter 1:14.
c2-2pe-0001: Peter recalls the Father speaking to honor Jesus. Let's read Second Peter 1:17.
c2-2pe-0002: Peter calls false teachers wells without water. Let's turn to Second Peter 2:17 and 19.
c2-2pe-0003: Peter says scoffers will come in the last days. Let's read Second Peter 3:3 and 4.
c3-2pe-0001: Those who do these things will never stumble. Let's check Second Peter 1:9 and 10.
c3-2pe-0002: Peter thinks it right to stir them up by reminding them. Let's read Second Peter 1:13 and 3:1.
c3-2pe-0003: Peter warns that false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies. Let's dig into Second Peter 2:1 and 3:17.
c3-2pe-0004: False teachers will exploit people with deceptive words. Let's read Second Peter 1:16 and 2:3.
